corrections.how:
Held by the asking parent's

-main. State: one project note (memory/projects/.md through the F041 write path, or home-store rows from F031) with goal, end date, decisions, open items and a review date. The note records only what the parent typed or confirmed, written in a turn that carried no web or research results. Check-ins: one isolated automation per project, created through the `automations` tool on

-main with a `pacing` object (`min`, `max`; `--pacing-min` and `--pacing-max` are the CLI spelling), so each run can call `automations(action: "next_check")` and be clamped to those bounds. The job's tool cap holds the note or home-store read tools plus `automations` (inside an automation run that tool is limited to the run's own job) and never `sessions_spawn` or a web tool; announce to the owner; NO_REPLY when nothing is due; the run removes its own job after the end date. Hard prerequisites before `automations` is allowed on

-main: the fail-closed before_tool_call pin must also match `automations`/`cron` add and update and refuse webhook delivery, completion and failure destinations, and any recipient other than the asking parent; and `cron.triggers.enabled: false`, so the tool does not offer script payloads, trigger scripts or stream commands. Research legs: `sessions_spawn` to the stateless `research` agent with `runTimeoutSeconds` and `completionTarget: "parent"`, in interactive turns only, so

-main reviews the result privately before it texts anything. Decisions are plain proposals in chat (or `ask_user` while the parent is in the conversation). `/goal` is not the durable state here (see AUT-02).
caveats: Scheduled runs do not get MEMORY.md injected, so a check-in must read the project note with a tool or carry the state in the job message.
A job created from chat is capped to the tools the creating turn had and cannot be widened later, so a check-in can never do more than the parent's own main agent.
The conversation resets every morning at 04:00 and that also wipes any /goal; the project note is the only continuity between days.
Every check-in is a cloud model turn. Pace in days, not minutes, and cap active projects per person (three is plenty).

The one long-task measurement opened in this run dates from March 2025 and covers software tasks: the frontier model of that time finished about half of the tasks that take a person roughly 50 minutes. It says nothing direct about gpt-6-sol or about family planning. The case for many short runs with a parent between them rests on cost and on keeping a person in the loop, not on that number.

Command-owner status is gateway-wide: an owner can ask their agent to list, inspect, update, run or remove any job on the gateway, whoever created it. Once Jordan is an owner, each parent's agent can read and change the other's check-in jobs, so job messages must not carry private detail.

The F041 plan refuses memory writes in a turn tainted by web results, and a turn that received a research result is tainted. Research findings therefore cannot be saved into the project note in that turn: they stay in the chat thread, and the note holds only what the parent states or confirms afterwards.
No bookings, purchases or invitations sent: the output is options, links and drafts. A static checklist is still easier in a shared Notes or Reminders list; Happy adds the nudging and the research.
corrections.safety:
-main holds the note and never browses; `research` does every web leg, has no memory, and as a sub-agent can never get the message, cron or gateway tools. The `automations` tool is itself a send path: a job can name any chat as its delivery target or post its result to a webhook URL.

Check-in runs carry no web tool and no `sessions_spawn`; that is the hard limit. The rule that handoff text carries dates, ages and budget only (never names, school or address) is prompt text, not enforcement. With the pin in place nothing on the never list is reachable: there is no payment, booking or outbound-to-strangers tool anywhere in the chain.

All ten sources check out, but a prerequisite is missing: the model loads a skill by reading its SKILL.md with the `read` tool, and

corrections.how:
Happy answers with the drafted procedure as plain text (no tool needed). Tony turns it into `skills//SKILL.md` (a `name` and a one-line `description`, optionally `user-invocable`) in happy-config under that person's template, reviews it, and happy-deploy copies it into that agent's workspace `skills/` folder, the highest-precedence skill root. To use a skill the model must load its SKILL.md with the `read` tool; the system prompt lists only each skill's name, description and location. So

-main needs `read` in `tools.alsoAllow` and in the sandbox tool allowlist (group:fs is denied today). With `workspaceAccess: "none"` OpenClaw mirrors eligible skills into the sandbox workspace as read-only copies and `read` is rooted there. Keep `skill_workshop` denied on every family agent. Alternative for agent-scoped Workshop skills: `openclaw skills workshop propose-create --agent

-main --proposal ./PROPOSAL.md`, then inspect and apply, run as the happy user from the deploy path. Per-agent visibility through `agents.entries..skills`; inbox keeps `skills: []`. Held by the asking parent's

-main; shared stateless agents get only skills meant for everyone. A routine of a few lines can instead live as a section of AGENTS.md, which needs no tool.
caveats: Asking Happy to save a skill from iMessage does not work on this stack by default: sandboxed runs do not construct the `skill_workshop` tool even when it is allowlisted, so `/learn` cannot stage a draft. The M1 doctor baseline in the config repo already shows this warning for every agent. The documented exception is a human turn with host-granted library-authoring authority, and personal-library authoring publishes with no pending draft, which would skip Tony's review. That is one more reason to keep `skill_workshop` off every family agent's allowlist.
A skill is know-how. It cannot add tools or accounts, so "learn to order the groceries" still ends at a list.
A skill is instruction text loaded into future sessions. One written from a pasted web page or an email is a stored injection, so author only from the parent's own words.
No marketplace skills: an audit reported by The Hacker News found 341 malicious entries among 2,857 ClawHub skills in early 2026.
A new or changed workspace skill is picked up on the next turn after the skills watcher sees the file change, or after the gateway restart that a deploy performs. No /new is needed.
Turnaround is "when Tony next deploys", not instant.
unverified: Whether a user-invocable skill command typed by an allowlisted non-owner iMessage sender is accepted on 2026.9.7.

That a `read`-only grant on a sandboxed

-main reaches the mirrored skills and nothing private; check at build time.
Whether an iMessage owner turn is ever given library-authoring authority on this configuration. If it is, an allowlisted `skill_workshop` could publish a skill with no review.

corrections.how: In happy-config: a global `cron.failureAlert` object routed to the operator's handle, so alerts do not fall back to each job's own announce target; `--timeout-seconds` and an explicit `--tools` cap on every job the G003 registry emits; `cron.skipMissedJobs: true` for recurring jobs; `cron.triggers.enabled: false`, set before any agent is given the `automations` tool and kept until F029 deliberately turns triggers back on. happy-inspect reads `openclaw automations list --all` to catch auto-disabled jobs. The healthchecks dead-man switch stays as the only signal for a Mac that is off. Gateway-level; no agent gains anything.
caveats: By default a failure alert goes to the failing job's own announce target, so Jordan would receive "job failed" texts for her jobs unless they are rerouted.
Alerts start after 2 failures in a row with a 1-hour cooldown; repeats with the same cause count as one incident and one recovery notice closes it.
A recurring job is switched off after 10 failures in a row and then disappears from the default job list.
Without a per-job timeout an isolated agent job is bounded only by a 60-minute watchdog.
Jobs run inside the gateway. After a reboot with FileVault locked nothing fires and nothing alerts, and by default the scheduler catches up on missed recurring runs later.
One-shot reminders still catch up after an outage even with skipMissedJobs set; a late reminder is sometimes worse than none.

Once

-main has the automations tool, the agent offers to turn a repeated request into a schedule and creates it enabled with an immediate test run. That is pleasant, but those jobs are not in the G003 registry, so the registry diff must tolerate or report them.

Trigger scripts and script payloads run with the owning agent's full tool policy, exec included, in the Code Mode executor, and the docs name `cron.triggers.enabled` as their only switch. With triggers on, the `automations` tool also offers the model script payloads, trigger scripts and stream commands. Set `cron.triggers.enabled: false` before any agent is given that tool (F007, AUT-01, AUT-03). This switches off the trigger-script design of F029 until triggers are deliberately turned back on.
